topic: a blueprint becoming a furnished bedroom
angle: A floor plan is not a pitch. Turn the PDF into a photoreal room buyers can picture themselves in.
palette: graphite and warm walnut with brass
visualSummary: Three numbered horizontal bands on the deep blue field. Band one shows a flat black and white floor plan of a bedroom. Band two shows the plan with the room type and style chosen. Band three shows the finished photoreal modern bedroom, walnut bed, graphite bedding, brass lamps.

copy.headline: The plan is not the pitch.

whyNow: Pre-construction and new-build inventory listed before furniture exists.
whyThisEarnsAClick: An agent holding an unbuilt unit has no photo at all, so the click is the only way to get one.

angle: Student housing is a listing category too, and the tools that stage it are the same ones.
visualSummary: One empty cinderblock dorm room at the top, then the same room below in an asymmetric grid staged three ways, each with a style pill and a one line caption.
whyNow: August is the student housing leasing peak.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It names a room type competitors do not support, so the curious click to check.

topic: one typed sentence a preset cannot express
angle: Presets cover the common case. The prompt bar covers the listing-specific one.
palette: ink black and oat with sage
visualSummary: One staged home office render marked with three numbered pins and a numbered legend beneath, each pin naming a detail that came from the typed request rather than the preset.

copy.headline: Type the thing a preset cannot say.

whyNow: Every agent has one listing detail no dropdown covers.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It answers the generic-AI objection with specifics, and specifics are what get tried.

topic: sending a broker a link that needs no account
angle: The seller sees the renders in one tap. No login, no app, no forwarded zip file.
visualSummary: Three numbered bands: the staged farmhouse dining room, a share link capsule, and a phone-shaped card showing the same render opened by the client.
whyNow: Sign-off delays are the slowest part of a listing week.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It solves the workflow problem, not the picture problem, which is the one agents complain about.

topic: the ways agents get staging disclosure wrong
angle: MLS and NAR want the label. Stagify puts it on before you download.
visualSummary: A staged farmhouse bedroom render with three numbered pins on the disclosure tag, the caption field and the image corner, and a numbered legend beneath naming the three mistakes.

copy.headline: Three ways the disclosure goes wrong.

whyNow: Disclosure complaints are the reputational risk agents actually fear.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Compliance anxiety converts better than beauty.

topic: the same studio running in eleven languages
angle: The product is not English only, and neither is the client list.
visualSummary: One empty office at the top, then a grid of the same render below with each tile pilled in a different language.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Agents with non-English clients have a concrete reason to open it.

topic: room types most staging tools refuse to touch
angle: Bathrooms, offices and dorms are where competitors stop and listings still need photos.
visualSummary: An empty office at the top, then a grid of harder room types staged below with a room pill on each tile.
whyNow: Listings are rarely one living room.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It reframes the buy from a picture to full coverage of a listing.

topic: listing photos ready before the furniture ships
angle: New builds list months before anything is delivered. The plan is enough to shoot from.
visualSummary: Three bands: a dining room floor plan, the settings row, then the finished scandinavian dining room.

copy.headline: List it before it is furnished.

whyNow: Autumn completions are being listed now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It names a deadline, and deadlines get acted on.

topic: the specific decisions inside one staged bedroom
angle: The furniture is chosen for the room, not dropped in. Here are three proofs in one frame.
visualSummary: A staged farmhouse bedroom with three numbered pins on scale, walkway clearance and window light, with a numbered legend beneath.
whyNow: The generic-AI objection is the standing sales objection.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It argues quality with evidence rather than an adjective.

topic: the compliance line an MLS expects on a staged photo
angle: Every render leaves with the label already applied. You cannot forget it.
visualSummary: A modern dining room render with two numbered pins on the stamped tag and the file corner, and a legend beneath.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Risk removal is a reason to sign up today.

topic: clients reviewing renders without signing up for anything
angle: Sign-off happens on a link. The seller never makes an account.
visualSummary: Three bands: staged office render, share capsule, client approval view.

copy.headline: Your seller will not make an account.

whyNow: Sellers abandon anything with a signup wall.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It removes the friction the agent gets blamed for.

topic: asking for a reading corner instead of picking a preset
angle: One sentence gets you the thing the listing actually needs.
visualSummary: A scandinavian bedroom render with pins on a reading chair, a floor lamp and a shelf, each named in the legend as part of the typed request.
whyNow: Prompt-driven tools are what buyers expect now.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It shows the request and the result in the same frame.

topic: student rentals that lease in a single august week
angle: Student housing turns over fast and photographs empty. Stage it in minutes.
visualSummary: Three numbered bands walking an empty dorm room through room type, style and finished render.
whyNow: Mid August is peak student move-in.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Time pressure plus a specific niche.

topic: one spare bedroom photographed as three uses
angle: Buyers cannot picture an empty box. Show them the options side by side.
visualSummary: Empty spare room at the top, three staged versions beneath in an asymmetric grid.
whyNow: Spare rooms are the hardest square footage to sell.
whyThisEarnsAClick: Breadth is the strongest proof the account has.

topic: a pdf floor plan and the dining room it becomes
angle: From a flat drawing to a photoreal room, with nothing shot on site.
visualSummary: A rendered dining room built from a plan, pinned where the plan dictated the window wall, the doorway and the table run, with the plan itself inset.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It shows an output an agent cannot get any other way.

topic: overseas buyers reading the studio in their own language
angle: Eleven languages means the client can use it too, not just you.
visualSummary: One empty bedroom above, the same render in a grid below with language pills.

copy.headline: Your buyer does not read English.

whyNow: Cross-border buying is a large share of high-end listings.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It gives the agent something to forward.

topic: the label most staging tools leave off entirely
angle: Automatic disclosure is a differentiator, not a chore.
palette: birch and off white with black
visualSummary: A scandinavian office render with a pin on the stamped disclosure tag and a legend explaining what it satisfies.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It sets a checkable standard the reader can go test.

topic: getting sign off from a seller in one tap
angle: The approval loop is the delay. A link closes it same day.
visualSummary: Three bands from render, to link, to an approved state.
whyThisEarnsAClick: It promises a measurable time saving.
